/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report - 26 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3152 (45)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5100 (86)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2273 (50)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1816 (2)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1083 (4)

CAPESIZE
The market extended its upward movement today, with the BCI 182 5TC adding a further $777 to close at $46,250, as continued strength in the Pacific once again underpinned the overall market. The C5 index edged up by $0.285 to $16.435, with two miners active alongside solid operator demand. The positive trajectory in the Pacific continued, with an operator initially bidding $16.00 against offers in the upper $16s for 12–16 December dates, before eventually fixing at $16.50. One miner was also reported to have paid $17.00 for an earlier 7–9 December arrival, followed by a further fixture at $16.25 basis 12–14 December. These fixtures underline the continued strength in the Pacific, with owners maintaining firm ideas. The South Atlantic remained lethargic, much as it has throughout the week, with limited activity and little fresh enquiry. The C3 index edged up just $0.150 to $35.409. Reports emerged of $35.70 having been paid last night, with brokers suggesting owners were prepared to repeat this level today, although a lack of bids kept activity subdued. In contrast, the North Atlantic maintained a positive tone, with firmer fixtures reported and sentiment continuing to improve. All in all, another positive day for the Capes, with the Pacific continuing to lead the way and provide solid support to the broader market, while the North Atlantic also showed encouraging signs. The South Atlantic remains the notable area of weakness, with activity yet to gather momentum.

PANAMAX
The market maintained its positive momentum today, with gains across both basins pushing the P5TC up by $447 to $20,456. In the Atlantic, brokers reported that prompt tonnage remained tight in the North, with adverse weather further restricting vessel availability, particularly for ships positioning towards the US East Coast. While additional tonnage has started to emerge from the West Mediterranean and West Africa for early December, continued Charterer interest in trans-Atlantic business has helped absorb these positions and maintain support for rates. Owners consequently remained firm in their expectations, with both trans-Atlantic and fronthaul activity continuing to underpin sentiment. Further South, market sources highlighted healthy demand for December dates, with a relatively restricted tonnage list allowing Owners to maintain their offers. In the Pacific, market participants reported further gains, although activity remained uneven across the region. In the North Pacific, prompt grain requirements continued to provide support, while adverse weather across North China disrupted vessel schedules and reduced the availability of suitably positioned ships, allowing Owners to push for higher rates. Australian rounds also strengthened, with improving demand and competition for available tonnage contributing to firmer fixing levels. Indonesian activity showed signs of improvement, with rates edging higher alongside the broader strengthening of the Pacific market.

SUPRAMAX
The combination of the Thanksgiving holiday and Geneva parties made for a quiet day, but the 11TC rose slightly again to settle at 22,950. North American rates have been very firm, and activity earlier in the week was obviously prompted by the holidays, so there were very few fresh rumours today. The South was said to be balanced with a reasonable amount of activity, which has seen market levels maintained, which has also been true for the Continent. The Mediterranean remains very subdued with very little of note being reported. Rates in Asia have bottomed out with the index now returning small positive gains amid light trading, but ships in the Indian Ocean are still finding life challenging, and are having to look to other markets for alteratives. The Elektra (63,638 2015) open prompt in South Africa fixed a trip via EC South America back to China with a reported duration of about 70 days at $27,000 to an unnamed source, and the Jaador (56,098 2013) Karachi 1-3 December was said to have fixed a trip back to South Korea at $11,000, but there were no further details.

HANDYSIZE
The market recorded another quiet day, with limited fresh information emerging. The BHSI increased by 4 points to 1,083, while the 7TC average rose by $59 to close at $19,486. In the Continent and Mediterranean, market fundamentals and rate levels remained largely unchanged, with many participants away from their desks attending events in Geneva. Despite limited reported fixtures, the US Gulf continued to strengthen, supported by healthy demand and a tight tonnage list as the Thanksgiving holiday approached. The South Atlantic remained steady but cautious, with rates discussed slightly below or around last-done levels. The Pacific market was mixed, although sentiment in North Asia appeared more positive, with active trading on North Pacific to Southeast Asia routes. The Woohyun Star (37,067 2013) open Gresik 30 November–2 December was fixed for an Australian round in the $18,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
HRB Steel Prices

In the two weeks to 25 November, the US hot-rolled band (HRB) steel price rose $129/t to $1,520/t, its highest since May 2022, World Steel Dynamics data show. The Western European HRB steel price edged $10/t higher to a three-year high of $855/t. In contrast, the Chinese domestic price eased $5/t to $409/t, its lowest since early March.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape saw a weaker session, with heavy morning activity followed by a gradual decline in the afternoon and further weakness into the close. Dec opened at 37,800, with significant early volume around 37,700–37,800, including two 120-lot prints. Prices settled around 37,500–37,650 before weakening throughout the afternoon, last trading at 36,900. Jan strengthened from 27,750 to 28,500 early before gradually easing to 28,000 late. Q1 27 remained steady at 26,700, with good morning volume, while Q3 27 weakened from 31,100 to 30,850. Cal 27 reached 29,900 before easing to 29,750, with 300 lots clearing at the lower level.
